Question: Why is Naomi Watts not a big star anymore? What happened?
Answer: She had kids. I was reading about her, she is still a big name, many producers still want her, but she wanted to give her childrens a “normal life". When she was kid she didn't have a predictable routine, and she missed that, she wanted “normal parents” and didn't want her kids to feel the same way. Question: What lesser known country would you recommend visiting?
Answer: Georgia. The country, not the state. It's not a very famous country (it's famous only of you live near it). The first time they had a huge press coverage was when they started the war against Russia. Before that I couldn't barely remember them, they have more famous neighbors like Armenia and Azerbaijan, at least I used to read about them more often. First time I noticed that I should pay more attention to them was when I was in Russia, Georgian cuisine and wines are very popular and appreciated by Russians. So I started to get curious. Another thing that helped is that I was living in Dubai and Georgia is a very popular cityscape there. They offer very good packages to travel there, be summer or winter. And many people always saying that it is an amazing country with good food. So I decided that my next winter would be snowboarding in Georgia. Arriving there I wasn't expecting the capital to be a beautiful city. The mountains, old churches, the rocks, river, waterfall in the city center. The hills they have in the other side of the river is fantastic. They have even more beautiful sights in the country side, an old civilization there, they claim to be the first place to produce wine, they also have one of the first Christian communities in the world. Believe me, the country is a gem. Leaving Tbilisi and going to the mountains, beautiful scenery, it was my first time going to real mountains to snowboard. I spent one week there, I wish I had reserved more days there. Pro tip: Visit there before it becomes a popular destination and prices will increase. It's really cheap to visit and you will have an amazing time there. The country is still more conservative than other European countries but it doesn't mean that they don't have typical scams at night. Keep that in mind. Question: What are some common scams in Hungary?
Answer: Although the consume girls (really overpriced drinks) are very common in Hungary, it did not happen to me. Budapest, 2012, the land of the scammers. A girl was robbed at same hostel that I was; the thieves had took her luggage. ALL her luggage. She was crying. From that I knew I wasn’t in the safest place in Europe. I was coming back from a pool party there (incredible, Budapest has really good parties) and there was huge line of people waiting for taxis. I and my friend were there waiting when suddenly comes a girl asking where we were going. She was a local girl and said she was going to the same direction and we would share the taxi. Nice, having a local is usually a good sign. Inside the car she started to “sleep” and leaning over our bodies. After a while I realized that the taximeter was like a chronometer, counting very fast. I was furious and demanded to stop, but was almost our destination and we had to pay a three times more than we paid when going to spa. Inside the hostel I realized I didn't have my smartphone anymore… my first night in Budapest. Another story is when me and my friend got caught inside the tram without tickets (I know is not correct, my friend insisted) the police first approached us inside the tram, as he knew that we didn’t have the tickets. He asked us to leave the tram at the next stop. He was saying that the fine was 50 euros, he had fill a huge form, take us to the police station, then started to ask from where we were. From Brazil, we said. He then starts to talk about football and how much he loves Brazil and because of that he would be nice to us, we just gave him all the money we had, about 20 euros each and he left. It took us more than one hour all that situation. This friend of mine was also scammed out trying to buy some weed on the streets and got some grass instead. And I was warning him about not buying on the streets because this is a very common scam. The guy approaches you, ask what do you want and go to pick it up. He them made us wait a lot of time. 20 min I think. Until you get angry, so when finally come back you are furious and in rush to leave. My friend got some grass. Budapest! But I loved the city, really. This same friend in Prague was scammed out in the same way the NatGeo “Scam City” had shown. But is a long story.
